judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY THREE Performance Objectives (same rank 2) under the same Topic '1. Symmetry', Sub-Theme 'Shapes', Theme 'Mensuration and Geometry'. First objective is 'identify the presence of straight lines and curves in real life situations'; second is 'identify shapes with line(s) of symmetry'. These are complementary geometric-recognition skills within one topic — recognizing lines/curves and identifying symmetric shapes reinforce shared understanding of shape/line features — showing substantive conceptual coherence. However, there is no clear directional dependency: identifying lines in real life is not a demonstrable prerequisite for identifying symmetry, and same-rank developmental direction lacks substantive evidence. Shared hierarchy, token overlap ('identify', 'pupils should be able to'), and page proximity alone do not establish a build direction, so relatesTo is the supported symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives (rank 0) sharing the same Theme (Number and Numeration) and Sub-Theme (Whole Number). The first, 'identify number of objects in a group or collection' (Topic 1, Whole numbers 1-5), is a foundational quantifying/counting skill; the second, 'recognize 10 as a group' (Topic 4, Whole number 10), extends the notion of a group to recognizing a set of ten as a unit, the basis for grouping and place value. Proficiency in identifying the number of objects in a group substantively supports recognizing 10 as a group, and the within-sub-theme topic ordering (Topic 1 to Topic 4) corroborates the lower-to-higher developmental direction. This is a pair-specific conceptual extension, not mere shared 'group'/'number' wording or hierarchy.
